questions.stem: In a physiology lab, a healthy 23-year-old student gives two saliva samples. The first is collected at rest, and the second while he sucks on lemon drops. Resting saliva: flow 0.3 mL/min, sodium 8 mEq/L, potassium 30 mEq/L, chloride 12 mEq/L. Stimulated saliva: flow 3 mL/min, sodium 75 mEq/L, potassium 20 mEq/L, chloride 50 mEq/L. Both samples are hypotonic to his plasma. Which best explains the higher sodium and chloride in the stimulated sample?
choices: Faster duct transit leaves less time to reabsorb sodium chloride
The acinar cells switch to secreting a hypertonic fluid during stimulation
Aldosterone release during stimulation increases ductal sodium secretion
The ducts become permeable to water, so water leaves the lumen
Ductal cells add sodium chloride to the lumen in exchange for potassium
questions.explanation: Acinar cells make a **plasma-like isotonic** fluid, and the **ducts**, which are nearly **impermeable to water**, then reabsorb Na+ and Cl- and add K+ and bicarbonate. At high flow, the fluid spends **less time in the ducts**, so its composition stays closer to plasma (more Na+ and Cl-, less K+), though it remains hypotonic. The water-permeability choice is tempting, but water-tight ducts are exactly why saliva is hypotonic; water leaving the lumen would make it more concentrated, not more plasma-like. Aldosterone acts on the ducts to increase Na+ **reabsorption**, which would lower salivary Na+.
questions.explanation_pt: As células acinares produzem um líquido **isotônico semelhante ao plasma**, e os **ductos**, quase **impermeáveis à água**, reabsorvem Na+ e Cl- e acrescentam K+ e bicarbonato. Com fluxo alto, o líquido passa **menos tempo nos ductos**, então sua composição fica mais próxima do plasma (mais Na+ e Cl-, menos K+), embora continue hipotônica. A alternativa da permeabilidade à água é tentadora, mas a impermeabilidade dos ductos é justamente o que torna a saliva hipotônica; a saída de água da luz a deixaria mais concentrada, e não mais parecida com o plasma. A aldosterona atua nos ductos aumentando a **reabsorção** de Na+, o que reduziria o Na+ salivar.

questions.stem: In a study of pancreatic secretion, a test solution is infused into the duodenum of a healthy volunteer through a tube, and pancreatic juice is collected from the pancreatic duct. During the infusion, juice volume rises several-fold. Its composition: sodium 150 mEq/L, potassium 5 mEq/L, bicarbonate 130 mEq/L and chloride 25 mEq/L. Output of amylase and trypsinogen barely changes from baseline. Which infused solution most likely produced this response?
choices: An emulsion of long-chain fatty acids
A mixture of amino acids and peptides
A concentrated glucose solution
Dilute hydrochloric acid
Isotonic sodium chloride
questions.explanation: **Acid** in the duodenum releases **secretin** from **S cells**. Secretin raises **cAMP** in pancreatic **duct cells**, which open **CFTR** and secrete bicarbonate through a Cl-/HCO3- exchanger, giving a large volume of **bicarbonate-rich, chloride-poor** juice with little enzyme. A fatty acid emulsion is the tempting choice, but fat acts mainly through **CCK**, which would sharply raise amylase and trypsinogen output from acinar cells. Isotonic saline in the duodenum gives no strong hormonal signal to the pancreas.
questions.explanation_pt: O **ácido** no duodeno libera **secretina** das **células S**. A secretina aumenta o **AMPc** nas **células ductais** do pâncreas, que abrem o **CFTR** e secretam bicarbonato por um trocador Cl-/HCO3-, gerando um grande volume de suco **rico em bicarbonato e pobre em cloreto**, com pouca enzima. A emulsão de ácidos graxos é a alternativa tentadora, mas a gordura atua sobretudo pela **CCK**, que aumentaria muito a saída de amilase e tripsinogênio pelas células acinares. A solução salina isotônica no duodeno não gera sinal hormonal forte para o pâncreas.

questions.stem: A healthy 30-year-old woman takes part in a study on two separate days. On day 1, she drinks a glucose solution. On day 2, glucose is given intravenously at a rate adjusted so that her plasma glucose curve matches day 1. At 30 minutes: day 1, plasma glucose 152 mg/dL and insulin 64 µU/mL; day 2, plasma glucose 150 mg/dL and insulin 26 µU/mL. C-peptide follows the same pattern as insulin. Which cells release a hormone that best explains the difference between the two days?
choices: G cells of the gastric antrum
K cells of the duodenum and jejunum
I cells of the duodenum and jejunum
S cells of the duodenum
D cells of the gastric antrum
questions.explanation: With matched glucose levels, the extra insulin (and C-peptide, so true beta-cell secretion) after oral glucose is the **incretin effect**. Glucose in the gut lumen releases **GIP** from **K cells** of the duodenum and jejunum (and GLP-1 from L cells), and these hormones **increase glucose-dependent insulin release**. **I cells** are the tempting choice because they are in the same segments, but they release CCK in response to fat and amino acids, not glucose. **D cells** release somatostatin, which inhibits insulin release.
questions.explanation_pt: Com níveis de glicose iguais, a insulina extra (e o peptídeo C, ou seja, secreção real pelas células beta) após a glicose oral é o **efeito incretina**. A glicose na luz intestinal libera **GIP** das **células K** do duodeno e do jejuno (e GLP-1 das células L), e esses hormônios **aumentam a liberação de insulina dependente de glicose**. As **células I** são a alternativa tentadora porque estão nos mesmos segmentos, mas liberam CCK em resposta a gordura e aminoácidos, não a glicose. As **células D** liberam somatostatina, que inibe a liberação de insulina.

questions.stem: A healthy 27-year-old man has antroduodenal manometry after an overnight fast. The recording shows a repeating cycle about every 100 minutes: a quiet period, then irregular contractions, then 5 to 10 minutes of strong contractions at the maximum rate that start in the gastric antrum and move down into the small intestine. The plasma level of one peptide peaks just before each burst that starts in the stomach. When he eats a meal, the cycle stops and is replaced by irregular contractions. Which peptide is it?
choices: Cholecystokinin
Secretin
Gastrin
Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide
Motilin
questions.explanation: This is the **migrating motor complex (MMC)**, the fasting pattern whose strong phase sweeps leftover food, secretions and bacteria toward the colon; loss of the MMC favors **small intestinal bacterial overgrowth**. Its gastric phase is coordinated by cyclic release of **motilin**, and **eating stops** both the cycle and motilin release. **Cholecystokinin** is the tempting choice because it is a duodenal motility hormone, but it is released by a meal and slows gastric emptying, which fits the fed state, not the fasting bursts.
questions.explanation_pt: Este é o **complexo motor migratório (CMM)**, o padrão do jejum cuja fase forte varre restos de alimento, secreções e bactérias em direção ao cólon; a perda do CMM favorece o **supercrescimento bacteriano do intestino delgado**. Sua fase gástrica é coordenada pela liberação cíclica de **motilina**, e **comer interrompe** tanto o ciclo quanto a liberação de motilina. A **colecistocinina** é a alternativa tentadora por ser um hormônio duodenal ligado à motilidade, mas é liberada pela refeição e retarda o esvaziamento gástrico, o que corresponde ao estado alimentado, e não às contrações do jejum.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man had a truncal vagotomy with pyloroplasty years ago for a bleeding duodenal ulcer. Since then, he feels full and uncomfortable after eating only small amounts. A gastric emptying study shows that liquids leave his stomach faster than normal. His symptoms are mainly due to loss of a vagovagal reflex that relaxes the proximal stomach as food arrives. Which signal from enteric neurons normally produces this relaxation?
choices: Acetylcholine acting on M3 receptors of smooth muscle
Substance P acting on neurokinin receptors of smooth muscle
Nitric oxide and VIP released onto smooth muscle
Norepinephrine acting on beta-2 receptors of smooth muscle
Serotonin acting on 5-HT4 receptors of enteric neurons
questions.explanation: Swallowing and food in the stomach trigger **receptive relaxation** (and accommodation) of the fundus and proximal body through a **vagovagal reflex**. The vagal fibers activate **inhibitory enteric neurons** that release **nitric oxide and VIP**, so the stomach holds a meal without a large rise in pressure. After vagotomy this reflex is lost, causing **early satiety** and fast emptying of liquids. Norepinephrine is the tempting choice because sympathetic input does relax gut muscle, but it is not the transmitter of this vagal reflex; acetylcholine and substance P are excitatory and cause contraction.
questions.explanation_pt: A deglutição e a chegada de alimento ao estômago desencadeiam o **relaxamento receptivo** (e a acomodação) do fundo e da parte proximal do corpo por um **reflexo vagovagal**. As fibras vagais ativam **neurônios entéricos inibitórios** que liberam **óxido nítrico e VIP**, e assim o estômago acomoda a refeição sem grande aumento de pressão. Após a vagotomia, esse reflexo se perde, causando **saciedade precoce** e esvaziamento rápido de líquidos. A noradrenalina é a alternativa tentadora porque a inervação simpática de fato relaxa o músculo intestinal, mas não é o transmissor desse reflexo vagal; a acetilcolina e a substância P são excitatórias e causam contração.

questions.stem: A strip of duodenal wall with intact muscle layers is taken from a surgical specimen and studied in an organ bath. Electrodes record rhythmic membrane depolarizations about 12 times per minute. The rhythm continues unchanged after tetrodotoxin and atropine are added to the bath. The strip contracts only when action potentials appear on top of a depolarization. Which cells most likely generate this rhythm?
choices: Neurons of the myenteric (Auerbach) plexus
Interstitial cells of Cajal
Neurons of the submucosal (Meissner) plexus
Enterochromaffin cells of the mucosa
Sympathetic postganglionic nerve endings
questions.explanation: These are **slow waves**, rhythmic oscillations of membrane potential made by the **interstitial cells of Cajal** and spread to smooth muscle through gap junctions. They set the **maximum contraction rate** of each segment (about 12/min in the duodenum), and contraction occurs only when spike potentials ride on them. Myenteric neurons are the tempting choice because they control the strength and pattern of motility, but **tetrodotoxin** blocks neuronal action potentials, so a rhythm that persists must come from non-neural pacemaker cells. Cajal cells express **c-KIT (CD117)**, which is why gastrointestinal stromal tumors, thought to arise from them, are KIT-positive.
questions.explanation_pt: Estas são **ondas lentas**, oscilações rítmicas do potencial de membrana geradas pelas **células intersticiais de Cajal** e transmitidas ao músculo liso por junções comunicantes. Elas definem a **frequência máxima de contração** de cada segmento (cerca de 12/min no duodeno), e a contração só ocorre quando potenciais em espícula surgem sobre elas. Os neurônios mioentéricos são a alternativa tentadora porque controlam a força e o padrão da motilidade, mas a **tetrodotoxina** bloqueia os potenciais de ação neuronais; portanto, um ritmo que persiste vem de células marca-passo não neurais. As células de Cajal expressam **c-KIT (CD117)**, e por isso os tumores estromais gastrointestinais, que parecem originar-se delas, são KIT-positivos.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man had a retroperitoneal lymph node dissection 3 weeks ago. Since he resumed a normal diet, his abdomen has grown larger. Paracentesis yields milky, odorless fluid. Fluid analysis: triglycerides 430 mg/dL (high), many lymphocytes, Gram stain negative. His team replaces most dietary fat with medium-chain triglycerides, and the fluid builds up much more slowly. Which property of medium-chain fatty acids best explains this benefit?
choices: They need more bile salt micelles than long-chain fatty acids do
They are stored in enterocytes until fasting begins
They block pancreatic lipase, so less fat is digested
They enter portal blood without being packed into chylomicrons
They are absorbed only in the terminal ileum
questions.explanation: Long-chain fatty acids are rebuilt into triglycerides in the enterocyte and packed with apoB-48 into **chylomicrons**, which leave through the **lacteals** into lymph; here that chyle leaks from injured lymphatics (**chylous ascites**). **Medium-chain fatty acids** are more water-soluble, so they leave the enterocyte directly into **portal blood**, bound to **albumin**, without chylomicron formation, which lowers lymph flow. The micelle choice is wrong in direction: medium-chain fats depend **less** on bile salts, which is also why they help patients with bile salt loss.
questions.explanation_pt: Os ácidos graxos de cadeia longa são reesterificados em triglicerídeos no enterócito e empacotados com apoB-48 em **quilomícrons**, que saem pelos **vasos quilíferos** para a linfa; aqui esse quilo extravasa de linfáticos lesados (**ascite quilosa**). Os **ácidos graxos de cadeia média** são mais hidrossolúveis, então saem do enterócito diretamente para o **sangue portal**, ligados à **albumina**, sem formar quilomícrons, o que reduz o fluxo linfático. A alternativa das micelas está na direção errada: as gorduras de cadeia média dependem **menos** dos sais biliares, e por isso também ajudam pacientes com perda de sais biliares.

questions.stem: A 3-week-old girl has had severe watery diarrhea and dehydration since her first feeds of breast milk. The stool is acidic and tests positive for reducing sugars. A lactose-free formula whose only carbohydrate is glucose polymers does not help. When she is switched to a formula whose only carbohydrate is fructose, the diarrhea stops within a day. Her liver size and urinalysis are normal. A defect in which protein best explains these findings?
choices: Lactase
Sucrase-isomaltase
GLUT2
GLUT5
SGLT1
questions.explanation: **Glucose and galactose** enter the enterocyte through the apical **Na+-glucose cotransporter SGLT1**; **fructose** uses **GLUT5**, a separate facilitated carrier. Loss of SGLT1 leaves glucose and galactose in the lumen, where they pull water osmotically and are fermented, so any formula containing them fails while a fructose-only formula works. **Lactase** deficiency is the tempting choice, but glucose polymers need no lactase and still caused diarrhea. A **GLUT2** defect would also block basolateral exit of fructose, and it affects the liver and kidney, which are normal here.
questions.explanation_pt: A **glicose e a galactose** entram no enterócito pelo **cotransportador Na+-glicose SGLT1** apical; a **frutose** usa o **GLUT5**, um transportador facilitado separado. A perda do SGLT1 deixa glicose e galactose na luz, onde atraem água por osmose e são fermentadas; assim, qualquer fórmula que as contenha falha, enquanto a fórmula só com frutose funciona. A deficiência de **lactase** é a alternativa tentadora, mas os polímeros de glicose não precisam de lactase e ainda assim causaram diarreia. Um defeito de **GLUT2** também bloquearia a saída basolateral da frutose e afetaria o fígado e o rim, que aqui estão normais.
